findings.evidence: NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO 430fe99 AND NOT A BLOCKER — recorded because it is the one thing in this review that did not reproduce as claimed, and silence about it would misrepresent how completely the claim was verified. The commit claims `bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter review-artifact-durability` under BD_SHIM_ONLY=1 goes pass=40 fail=1 rc=1 -> pass=41 fail=0 rc=0. In cwp-l1-repro:full (-u 1000:1000, BD_SHIM_ONLY=1, en_US.UTF-8, and separately re-run with CI's exact GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL identity step) I measured pass=38 fail=3 -> pass=39 fail=2 instead. The two extra failures are 'Leg C RESTORE: the canonical path DOES enter the tracker (step 5, green)' (expected 1, actual 0) and 'Leg C RESTORE: precondition — approve succeeds'. ATTRIBUTION IS NEVERTHELESS CLEAN AND MEASURED: `diff` of the FAIL-line sets before (752270c) and after (430fe99) removes EXACTLY one line, 'Leg A / AC-3: ...and says so by name', and changes nothing else — the two Leg C failures are present IDENTICALLY in both trees, so they are pre-existing and independent of this change. And they do not occur on the release gate: CI run 36458045072 job 109049319338 (L2, a8e9827) shows all three 'Leg C RESTORE' assertions PASS and AC-3 as the SOLE failure, with that job's own `__SPEC_SUMMARY__ pass=40 fail=1` matching the commit's before-number exactly. Instrumented the cause rather than guessing: the checkpoint commit at :467-468 that exists to defeat this very failure DID run and DID succeed (rc=0, measured by surfacing the rc the `>/dev/null 2>&1 || true` normally swallows), yet the fresh artifact still never entered the tracker — the tracker at the assertion held only `src/c-restore.ts`, and the canonical path `/tmp/component-fixture.*/docs/reviews/*-r1.json` was absent. That is the 94d.1 baseline-vs-raw-porcelain-line interaction the spec's own :449-465 comment describes and claims to have fixed.
findings.description: So the commit's DELTA claim is true and reproduced; its ABSOLUTE before/after numbers are true on the runner (verified from the job log) but not reproducible in a CI-matched container. The residual is that Leg C RESTORE carries an environment-sensitive assumption about how git collapses a wholly-untracked directory in porcelain output relative to a previously-captured baseline — the same class as the 12.47e finding from round 1: an assertion whose outcome depends on the environment, where single-run evidence should not be read as deterministic. Worth its own task alongside d73j rather than blocking this approval: the change set is green on the gate that governs the release, and nothing in this wave or in 430fe99 causes it.
